lead: The day after the Sacred Heart of Jesus, the Church honours the Immaculate Heart of his mother. In Isaiah, the people God has blessed rejoice like a bride adorned with jewels: “I will greatly rejoice in the Lord.” In the Gospel the twelve-year-old Jesus stays behind in the Temple, and Mary and Joseph search for him for three days. When they find him, he speaks of his Father, and Mary treasures all these things in her heart. The canticle of Hannah gives the response: “My heart exults in the Lord.”

r.h: Clothed with the garments of salvation
set: Chapters 56–66 of Isaiah come from the time after the return from exile in Babylon, when Jerusalem was being rebuilt in poverty and hope. Many scholars call this part of the book “Third Isaiah”. Chapter 61 begins with the words Jesus read in the synagogue at Nazareth: “The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed” (61:1; Luke 4:18).
Our verses close the chapter. God promises that his people will be known among the nations as blessed, and the city, or the prophet in her name, answers with a song of joy.
str: v. 9: the blessed people will be known among the nations.
v. 10: the song of joy: clothed with salvation, like a bridegroom and a bride.
v. 11: as a garden makes seeds spring up, so God will make righteousness spring up before the nations.
kw: A doubled verb for great joy. The same joy will sound in Mary’s Magnificat: “my spirit rejoices in God my Savior” (Luke 1:47).
Salvation is pictured as clothing that God himself puts on his people. It is his gift, not their own making.
God’s faithful, saving justice, which makes things right. Here it grows like a plant from the soil.
vv: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my whole being shall exult in my God;
The Church hears in these words the voice of Mary, who rejoiced in God her Saviour.
he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
Bride and bridegroom: the image of the covenant between God and his people. Mary, adorned with grace from the first moment of her life, is the first fruits of this wedding joy.
so the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.
What God sows in secret grows into praise that all can see.
ch: The Church applies this song to Mary, who was clothed with the garment of salvation from the first moment of her conception, preserved from every stain of original sin by the merits of Christ her Son (CCC 491–492). The opening words of the entrance antiphon of the Mass of the Immaculate Conception on 8 December are taken from this verse. Mary’s holiness is God’s gift, and her joy is the joy of one who knows that everything she has is grace.

r.h: His mother treasured all these things in her heart
set: This is the last scene of Luke’s infancy story and the only story in the Gospels from the hidden years of Jesus between his infancy and his public ministry. Devout Jewish families went up to Jerusalem for the great feasts, above all Passover. At twelve, a boy was approaching the age when he would take on the duties of the Law.
Pilgrims travelled in large groups of relatives and neighbours, which explains how Mary and Joseph could travel a day without noticing that Jesus was not with them.
str: vv. 41–42: the yearly pilgrimage; Jesus is twelve.
vv. 43–45: Jesus stays behind; his parents search for him.
vv. 46–47: after three days they find him among the teachers.
vv. 48–50: Mary’s question; Jesus speaks of his Father; they do not understand.
v. 51: Jesus returns to Nazareth and is obedient; Mary treasures all in her heart.
kw: Literally “in the things of my Father”. It can mean his Father’s house or his Father’s affairs. Both are true: the first words of Jesus in Luke speak of God as his Father.
A strong word for anguish. Mary and Joseph feel real pain; holiness does not make them stop being parents.
To keep carefully, to hold on to. Mary keeps the events and the words in her heart, even when she does not understand them, and ponders them (compare 2:19).
vv: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Many readers since early times have seen in the “three days” a foreshadowing of the three days in which Jesus was lost to his mother in death and found again in the Resurrection.
Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.
Mary calls Joseph his father. Jesus’ answer gently points to his other Father. Both are true: Joseph is his father in the eyes of the law and in love; God is his Father by nature.
Did you not know that I must be in my Father’s house?
The little word “must” will return in Luke for the divine plan that leads to the Cross (9:22; 24:26).
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
The Son of God lives thirty years of obedience in an ordinary home. Mary’s heart is the place where the mystery is kept and pondered.
ch: The Catechism teaches that the finding in the Temple is the only event that breaks the silence of the Gospels about the hidden years of Jesus, and that in it he lets us glimpse the mystery of his total consecration to a mission flowing from his divine sonship (CCC 534). His hidden life at Nazareth allows everyone to enter into fellowship with Jesus by the most ordinary events of daily life (CCC 533). The Second Vatican Council sees Mary as the one who “kept these things in her heart”, advancing in her pilgrimage of faith (Lumen Gentium 57–58). Her Immaculate Heart is a heart wholly open to God, keeping his word and bringing it to fruit.

qa: What does the Church mean by the “Immaculate Heart” of Mary?

The heart, in the Bible, is the centre of the person. Mary’s heart is called immaculate because she was preserved from all sin from the first moment of her existence and lived wholly for God. Devotion to her Immaculate Heart honours her inner life of faith, love and pondering, and asks her to lead us to her Son. It always points to Christ, as her own words did: “Do whatever he tells you” (John 2:5).
rite: Devotion to the heart of Mary was promoted in the seventeenth century by St John Eudes. After the appearances of Our Lady at Fatima in 1917, Pope Pius XII consecrated the world to the Immaculate Heart of Mary in 1942 and extended the feast to the whole Church in 1944. Pope St John Paul II made it an obligatory memorial, kept on the Saturday after the Solemnity of the Sacred Heart. This year it falls on the same day as the memorial of St Boniface (died 754), the English monk Wynfrith who became the apostle of Germany and was martyred at Dokkum in Frisia while preparing new Christians for confirmation. Both may be remembered today.
study: Mary did not understand, yet she kept the words in her heart. What word of God am I being asked to keep and ponder, without understanding it yet?
Jesus lived obediently at Nazareth for many years. How can the ordinary duties of my home become a place of holiness?
